key_insight: Low DFT energy and force errors do not guarantee reliable disordered-carbon simulations; MACE-MH-1 was the most consistently robust model tested.
engineering_relevance: Foundation interatomic potentials can support nanoporous-carbon modelling, but require application-specific checks of dynamical stability and structural accuracy.
method: Screen six foundation MLIPs using DFT energy and force errors and binding curves.
Test four models with melt-quench-anneal molecular dynamics.
Evaluate structural observables in pure and O/H-containing disordered carbons.
evidence_signal: All four MD-tested models reproduced principal experimental and specialised-potential signatures of nanoporous carbon, while O/H incorporation shifted pore-size distributions towards larger pores.
watch_item: Binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories exposed unphysical extrapolation and dynamical failures missed by low DFT errors, so benchmark accuracy alone is insufficient for model selection.
paper_title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons
